data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"An idempotent operation satisfies f(f(x))=f(x): repeated application converges to the same state as a single application. A safe operation merely guarantees that retries do not violate system invariants\u2014it need not produce identical state, only correct state. An append-only event log requires safety of its writers, not idempotency, because append is inherently non-idempotent (appending event E twice yields [E,E], not [E]). The log survives at-least-once delivery by making retries safe through deterministic operation identifiers or deduplication keys, not by making the append operation itself idempotent.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log has no deduplication layer and consumers cannot tolerate duplicate events, then safety alone is insufficient and the system cannot survive at-least-once delivery","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the deduplication key is not deterministic (e.g., a random UUID per attempt), retries produce distinct keys and the log cannot distinguish duplicates from genuinely new events","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the event payload itself is non-deterministic (e.g., includes wall-clock timestamps), then even with deduplication keys, replay may diverge because the first-delivered copy differs from the retried copy","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The append operation mutates the log by adding an entry. Calling append(E) twice produces two entries, violating f(f(x))=f(x). However, the writer can attach a deterministic, content-derived or operation-ID-based key to each event. On replay or retry, the log layer (or a downstream deduplication filter) recognizes duplicate keys and discards redundant entries. The system-level invariant\u2014deterministic replay producing identical derived state\u2014is preserved because the deduplication mechanism is itself idempotent, even though the raw append is not. Thus writers must be retry-safe (their retries produce detectable duplicates), and the log achieves safety, not idempotency, at the operation level.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
